subject: Implementation pulse: AtlasCloud dedicated GPU pool & regional routing decisions
messages:

Subject: Implementation kickoff: dedicated GPU pool + region questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great chemistry with your infra team. Per our call I wanted to kick off the implementation thread for the AtlasCloud dedicated capacity project (deal AC-4821). Attached is the initial SOW and a first-pass capacity proposal. Before we lock dates I need two quick confirmations from your side so the internal provisioning plan can be finalized: 

1) Region preference: you mentioned EU for data residency — do you want us to provision primary capacity in eu-west-1 (Ireland) or eu-central-1 (Frankfurt)? We recommend eu-west-1 for lower median latency to your app endpoints but eu-central-1 can be preferable for certain regulatory setups.

2) Burst profile: can you share expected peak QPS and the duration of typical bursts (minutes vs hours)? In our model this affects baseline reserved pool size vs burst capacity we put on autoscale.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm region & burst profile (reply here)
- 30-minute alignment call w/ Rishi + Vivek next week to review autoscale policy draft
- Sign SOW and provision a staging pool (estimated 3 business days after sign)

Attachments: AtlasCloud_initial_SOW_v1.pdf, atlas_capacity_proposal_v2.xlsx

Thanks,

Monica,

Thanks — quick answers below: 
- Region: please provision primary in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Our compliance team is pushing for that region due to data processing agreements for our EU customers.
- Burst profile: typical operational traffic is ~120 r/s steady-state for vector queries. We see bursts up to 1,200 r/s but those are short-lived (usually 5–20 minutes) tied to nightly batch jobs and sync bursts.

Also: SLA & procurement note — Procurement will want clear fallbacks and estimated cost for peak-day usage. I’ll loop Carlos for that part.

Happy to do a call next week — afternoons CET are easiest.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: dedicated GPU pool + region questions

Hi Sofia / Monica,

Thanks for the burst numbers, that helps a lot. High-level recommendation for AtlasCloud based on the 120 r/s steady / 1,200 r/s 5–20m bursts: 

- Baseline reserved pool: 6 A100-equivalent slots (sized for 120 r/s steady with modest batching).
- Burst capacity: set autoscale to allow up to 18 slots (3x baseline) for short bursts; autoscale policy should have a fast scale-up (30–60s) and controlled scale-down with a 10-minute cool-down to avoid oscillation.
- Preemptible/spot usage: we can route 40% of burst capacity to spot instances to save cost, with immediate fallback to reserved slots on spot revocation.
- Fallback region: we recommend eu-west-1 as secondary for cross-region failover — warm standby (minimal reserved), with automated routing policy to failover when latency or capacity SLOs breach for longer than 2 minutes.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for your common prompt patterns — this will reduce token costs and reduce burst load by ~20% in our estimates.

I’ve attached a short summary PDF for the autoscale policy and included a sample scaling curve in the capacity workbook. Questions for AtlasCloud:
1) Are you comfortable with a 10-minute scale-down cool-down?
2) Is routing to spot-derived instances allowed under your procurement/security rules?
3) Any hard SLA targets for p50/p95 latency we should bake into routing?

Next step: schedule 30m technical alignment. Monica — can you propose two slots Wed/Thu CET?

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood_autoscale_policy_summary.pdf]

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@atlascloud.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia@atlascloud.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 14:17:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: dedicated GPU pool + region questions

Team,

Appreciate the recommendations. A few procurement/security items before we lock on autoscale/spot strategies: 
- SLA: procurement would like an outline of guaranteed throughput and an explicit failover behavior when spot capacity is lost. Can you provide a short doc that states expected behavior for a spot failure during a 15-minute sustained burst?
- Security: we need to ensure that any spot nodes still meet our node attestation & image signing requirements. Does Redwood support signed images and attestation hooks for spot instances?
- Cost transparency: please provide a sample worst-case cost for a 24-hour sustained 18-slot run at our configuration so we can budget for peak-day scenarios.

Also: we have a security engineer (remote) who wants to review SOC2 artifacts — I have a link but it’s internal. Sofia will coordinate sharing.

-Carlos
Head of Procurement, AtlasCloud

Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: AtlasCloud dedicated GPU pool & regional routing decisions — summary & next steps

Hi all,

Thanks for the input — summarizing action items and logistics so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Action items (owners & target dates):
- Redwood to produce a 1-page "Spot failure behavior" doc that details failover sequencing and expected client-visible degradation (owner: Rishi) — due 2027-10-14.
- Redwood to confirm signed image + attestation support for spot nodes and provide a short integration checklist (owner: Vivek) — due 2027-10-15.
- Redwood to provide a sample worst-case cost calc for 24h at 18 slots (owner: Hannah) — due 2027-10-14.
- AtlasCloud to share SOC2 evidence link and security reviewer contact (owner: Sofia) — due 2027-10-12.
- Monica to schedule the technical alignment call (30m CET) — meeting invite sent for 2027-10-13 15:00 CET / 06:00 PT.

Decisions captured:
- Primary region: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt); fallback: eu-west-1 (Ireland) warm standby.
- Baseline/reserved pool: 6 slots; burst up to 18 with 30–60s scale-up and 10-minute cool-down.
- Spot usage allowed up to ~40% of burst capacity, with explicit fallback to reserved on revocation.

Attachments & links included: AtlasCloud_initial_SOW_v1.pdf, atlas_capacity_proposal_v2.xlsx, redwood_autoscale_policy_summary.pdf, SOC2 artifacts (Sofia to share).

Let me know if anything is missing. Looking forward to the call — Rishi and Vivek will walk through the autoscale curve and the failover playbook.

Thanks,
